check: On a foldable, complete checkout in book and tabletop postures and confirm the hinge, taskbar, and split-screen divider never cover totals or the pay button.
why_forgotten: Width matrices treat a foldable as a tall phone or a small tablet.

check: On a phone, focus the last checkout fields and confirm errors and the submit button stay visible above the virtual keyboard, notch, and home indicator.
why_forgotten: Screenshot passes run with the keyboard closed and no safe-area inset.

check: Run picking, row menus, filters, and tooltips on a touch tablet using tap and long-press only.
why_forgotten: Desktop automation and hover screenshots make pointer-only actions look done.

check: Autofill login, NIP, address, and phone from the browser and a password manager and confirm controlled fields and checksum validation accept the values.
why_forgotten: Tests type character by character and never fire autofill events.

check: Send a fast keyboard-wedge burst plus Enter into a picking quantity and confirm it commits once and does not submit or duplicate the order.
why_forgotten: Warehouse hardware input is outside the browser device lab.

check: Refresh, go back, rotate, and let the session expire mid-order, then confirm the cart is recoverable and a second order is not created.
why_forgotten: Happy-path suites always submit a clean, still-authenticated form.

check: Sign out on a shared tablet and confirm the next person cannot open the previous cart, prices, or pages from the back-forward cache.
why_forgotten: Each automated role gets a fresh browser profile.

check: Place an order with keyboard only and a screen reader, including combobox, date picker, dialog, and the return from Tpay.
why_forgotten: axe inspects static DOM and never drives widgets or speech.

check: Confirm every dialog traps and restores focus, every input has a programmatic name, and an invalid submit moves focus to a Polish error summary linked to the fields.
why_forgotten: Assertions check that error text exists somewhere on the page.

check: At 400% zoom, in dark mode, with forced-colors and reduced motion, confirm status is not color-only and checkout needs no two-dimensional scroll.
why_forgotten: Gates stop at axe contrast on one light-mode screenshot.

check: Read a PDF invoice and the plain-text email with a screen reader and confirm reading order, language pl, and totals are present without the images.
why_forgotten: Accessibility scope is limited to HTML pages that axe can crawl.

check: Measure INP while filtering, selecting, and editing a production-sized order grid on a mid-range Android phone.
why_forgotten: Lab checks track LCP and CLS on a small fixture.

check: Leave the warehouse or admin SPA open for a full shift with polling and confirm memory, timers, and duplicate requests stay bounded.
why_forgotten: CI sessions last seconds, so leaks never surface.

check: Deploy while a session is open and confirm stale chunks recover, and confirm CDN or SW caches never serve one role's or user's JSON to another.
why_forgotten: Tests always cold-load a bundle that matches the server.

check: Generate a large XLSX and a multi-page PDF during checkout and confirm export work uses a queue, a memory cap, and does not starve order requests.
why_forgotten: Functional fixtures are tiny and finish inside the web request.

check: On a production-volume copy, explain product and contractor search for unaccented and leading-substring Polish queries and confirm an index is used.
why_forgotten: Staging data is small enough that a sequential scan feels fine.

check: Call every order, invoice, attachment, and export URL as customer, sales rep, warehouse, accountant, and admin and confirm each id is limited to that role's scope.
why_forgotten: New agent endpoints authenticate the caller and skip object ownership.

check: Post extra fields for role, price, discount, payment status, and ERP id and confirm each role's allowlist drops them.
why_forgotten: Tests send the exact payload the UI builds.

check: Change or revoke a role, disable a user, and confirm the next request and the existing SPA session lose access without waiting for token expiry.
why_forgotten: The permission matrix is checked only at login.

check: Reject Tpay notifications with a bad signature, stale timestamp, reused id, or amount, currency, or order id that differs from the stored order.
why_forgotten: Sandbox tests accept any success callback.

check: Return from Tpay as a cross-site request and confirm the session survives SameSite rules and the paid order is not opened for a different browser.
why_forgotten: Local checkout never crosses a real third-party site boundary.

check: Prefetch activation, password-reset, and order links the way Outlook Safe Links does and confirm the real user can still complete them once.
why_forgotten: Developers open each link once in a normal browser.

check: Sync product, contractor, and note fields containing markup from ExampleERP and confirm UI, email, and PDF encode them.
why_forgotten: ERP data is treated as a trusted system of record.

check: Reject or neutralize spreadsheet formulas, XML external entities, zip-slip imports, and HTML content types on every export and import path.
why_forgotten: File tests open a benign sample and check column values.

check: Confirm tokens and NIPs stay out of query strings, Referer, access logs, source maps, and client bundles, and confirm debug consoles and seed passwords are absent in production.
why_forgotten: The flow works in the browser while secrets leave through side channels.

check: Require step-up authentication, a reason, and an audit event for impersonation and for exporting the full customer or order set.
why_forgotten: Role tests cover ordinary CRUD, not break-glass paths.

check: Run an erasure request and confirm contact data is anonymized while invoices and payment records stay intact for the statutory accounting period.
why_forgotten: Delete-account work collides with a five-year invoice duty and is postponed.

check: Inspect logs, traces, visual-regression screenshots, session replay, and agent fixtures for names, NIP, email, phone, address, and order notes.
why_forgotten: QA and error tools capture full pages by default.

check: Confirm staging restores and agent environments use anonymized data and cannot reach production ExampleERP, Tpay, or SMTP.
why_forgotten: A realistic copy quietly becomes a second production.

check: Compare the privacy notice, cookie list, and retention schedule with actual subprocessors, regions, employee admin telemetry, and log storage.
why_forgotten: Legal text is written once and the vendor list keeps changing.

check: Sort and search ą, ć, ę, ł, ń, ó, ś, ź, and ż in NFC and NFD and confirm the chosen alphabet order and accent folding.
why_forgotten: Database and UI collations are exercised with ASCII.

check: Render dates as DD.MM.YYYY in Europe/Warsaw, numbers as 1 234,56, PLN with zł, Monday-first calendars, genitive month names, and a delivery slot across the DST change.
why_forgotten: The server locale stays en-US and screenshots hide the exported values.

check: Round-trip NIP, REGON, postal code, phone, EAN, and NRB through forms, CSV, and XLSX without scientific notation, dropped zeros, or a failed checksum.
why_forgotten: JavaScript and Excel treat long digit strings as numbers.

check: Format 1, 2, and 5 orders with Polish plural rules and print the invoice total in words with correct złoty and grosz forms.
why_forgotten: English plural logic and a numeric total look sufficient.

check: Round-trip Polish text through the real ExampleERP encoding, reject mojibake, and strip control characters that would break the SOAP or XML payload.
why_forgotten: Stubs return clean UTF-8 while production still speaks Windows-1250.

check: Calculate dispatch and payment due dates with Polish public holidays, warehouse cutoffs, and a Monday week start.
why_forgotten: Date widgets default to Sunday and a generic weekend rule.

check: Open the order mail in Outlook desktop, Gmail, and WP.pl or Onet, in light and dark mode, with images blocked and a matching plain-text part.
why_forgotten: The HTML file is reviewed in Chrome.

check: Send seed mail and confirm SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment, inbox placement, diacritics in the From name, and a handled bounce.
why_forgotten: The staging SMTP sink accepts every message.

check: Open the XLSX in Polish Excel and confirm text NIPs, real date types, Polish number formats, frozen headers, stable columns, and no hidden cost sheet.
why_forgotten: CI checks that a file exists and has the expected headers.

check: Fail the SMTP connection after acceptance and confirm a retry cannot send customer A's attachment to customer B or send a second copy.
why_forgotten: The happy path sends one message to one inbox.

check: Confirm RFC 5987 filenames with diacritics, the real XLSX media type, nosniff, and a defined failure at the mailbox size limit.
why_forgotten: Dev catchers accept small ASCII filenames.

check: Print a long order to A4 and confirm repeating headers, unsplit rows, totals on the last page, embedded Polish glyphs, and readable grayscale.
why_forgotten: Responsive on-screen layout is what the visual gate captures.

check: Confirm the customer PDF omits margins and internal notes, the picking sheet omits prices, and the archive file is tagged PDF/A without private metadata or scripts.
why_forgotten: One HTML template is copied for every audience.

check: Confirm admin, account, order, and staging URLs are noindex and disallowed, and that any public share card cannot reveal order or customer data.
why_forgotten: A login wall is assumed to be equivalent to noindex.

check: With non-essential cookies rejected, confirm no analytics or replay call fires, and confirm a paid order counts once when both return URL and webhook succeed.
why_forgotten: Tags are verified in an already-consented profile, one path at a time.

check: Confirm events carry role and internal id only, and confirm payment and magic-link URLs do not send tokens or NIP to analytics.
why_forgotten: Debug payloads are copied into the production tracker.

check: Trigger a browser, API, and ERP failure and confirm one correlation id and release version, a Polish customer message, and no stack trace or PII.
why_forgotten: The SDK is installed and the failure path is never asserted.

check: Alert when ExampleERP or Tpay returns a transport success with a business rejection, even if trace sampling is low.
why_forgotten: Dashboards watch HTTP 5xx and treat 200 as healthy.

check: Restore the latest backup into isolation, record RPO and RTO, and reconcile orders, payments, files, and sequences with the source.
why_forgotten: A successful backup job is treated as proof of restore.

check: Confirm PDFs, XLSX, KSeF XML, and secrets needed to read encrypted backups are restorable and access-controlled.
why_forgotten: The database dump is scheduled and object storage is omitted.

check: Run the old app on the new schema and the new app on the old schema, then roll back a failed migration without losing orders placed during the window.
why_forgotten: Staging applies the migration and deploys one version.

check: Rehearse backfills on a production-sized copy and confirm they are idempotent and do not rewrite issued invoices, numbers, or stored totals.
why_forgotten: Agent migrations are tested on an empty database.

check: Limit login, NIP lookup, search, export, and mail per user and per real client IP, and confirm a spoofed forwarding header cannot reset the counter.
why_forgotten: Only the login form gets a limiter.

check: On ExampleERP and Tpay timeouts and 429s, retry with jitter, open a circuit, and show a Polish degraded state instead of a retry storm.
why_forgotten: Stubs never fail slowly or return 429.

check: Run two instances across a Warsaw DST change and confirm exports, dunning, and ERP sync execute once at the intended local time.
why_forgotten: Cron is verified on one developer process in UTC.

check: Complete checkout on the oldest supported warehouse Chrome, current Safari iOS, and Firefox, including ITP, private mode, and back-forward cache.
why_forgotten: CI runs one Chromium version.

check: Queue an order offline, restore the network twice, and confirm exactly one order is created and the service worker does not reveal the previous user's cache.
why_forgotten: Offline checks cover a banner, not replay and cache partitioning.

check: Install the PWA on iOS and confirm storage eviction, missing web push, and an update after deploy are handled without a stuck shell.
why_forgotten: Installability is tested on desktop Chromium.

check: For a new warehouse order and a payment result, confirm email, push, and in-app alerts respect preferences and produce one action, with a deep link that survives login.
why_forgotten: Each channel is demonstrated alone.

check: Reject non-essential cookies and confirm they stay off, and confirm regulamin acceptance stores user, time, and policy version and blocks checkout when the version changes.
why_forgotten: A banner click and a static terms page are checked once.

check: Validate the current FA schema, submit, store the UPO, show the QR visualization, and issue a correction that references the original KSeF id.
why_forgotten: PDF invoices ship first and e-invoicing stays a side project.

check: For invoices at the split-payment threshold, confirm MPP marking, the NRB checksum, and a VAT-account whitelist result before a transfer is instructed.
why_forgotten: Online Tpay coverage hides high-value bank-transfer rules.

check: Confirm a posted invoice cannot be edited or deleted, a later contractor rename does not change it, and a refund creates a correction.
why_forgotten: CRUD permissions are reused for legal documents.

check: Follow one order across web, mail, Tpay, and ExampleERP with a shared id and alert when sync lag or the unpaid-but-charged queue breaks its SLO.
why_forgotten: Each integration has its own log and no business SLO.

check: Run a synthetic login and order probe per role after deploy, and confirm a kill switch stops ExampleERP and mail side effects without blocking read-only work.
why_forgotten: Health checks only request the login page.

check: Store money in grosze or decimal, apply Polish per-line VAT rounding, and reject an order whose total differs from the sum of lines.
why_forgotten: Float totals match on small demo orders.

check: Crash after payment and before ERP or mail commit, replay the webhook and the outbox, and confirm one payment capture, one ExampleERP document, and one email.
why_forgotten: Each step's unit test commits its own happy path.

check: Reserve the last unit, expire a stale reservation, accept kg precision, and confirm the order keeps the price snapshot rather than today's catalog price.
why_forgotten: Catalog tests use unlimited integer stock and live prices.

check: Run the daily tie-out of panel totals, Tpay settlements, and ExampleERP documents and alert on any grosz difference or unmatched payment.
why_forgotten: Success of each API call is taken as end-to-end agreement.

check: Assert an explicit allow and deny for every role against orders, margins, exports, refunds, master data, and direct API calls, including hidden export columns.
why_forgotten: A new feature is clicked through as admin and the buttons are hidden for others.

check: Block a sales rep from overriding price or credit hold alone, and require a second person plus an audit record above the configured threshold.
why_forgotten: Functional tests grant the acting user every permission they need.

check: Submit the same cart from two tabs and let two sessions buy the last unit, and confirm one winner, one stock figure, and no duplicate payment.
why_forgotten: Load scripts use read-only browsing or a single user.

check: During a month-end export and an ExampleERP slowdown, confirm checkout keeps its pool, statement timeout, and replica read-your-writes behavior.
why_forgotten: Average-load tests run against an idle staging database.

check: Normalize NIP with PL, dashes, and non-breaking spaces, and confirm a retry updates the same ExampleERP contractor and never drops a line silently.
why_forgotten: Mapping is checked on one clean sandbox contractor.

check: Park a permanently rejected ERP order on a dead-letter queue with a visible reason, and confirm the rest of the queue keeps moving.
why_forgotten: Queue consumers are tested with valid messages only.

check: Close the tab during 3DS, deliver the webhook before the browser returns, and confirm pending, paid, failed, and refunded states stay consistent.
why_forgotten: The test waits for the webhook and the redirect in the expected order.

check: Review new agent changes for mocked integration boundaries, client/server validation drift, missing audit logs, hardcoded en-US formats, and secrets in fixtures.
why_forgotten: Generated tests pass while asserting the mock the agent also wrote.
